lyrics:
There's a model man

New shirt, new tie, and there he stood
the one they cleared a path to greet
They said that he was that good —
so good that good felt obsolete

I watched him round the numbers down
a wedding ring slipped in his coat
He leaned too close to the new girl in town
and nobody bothered to make a note

There's a model man
polished front, no visible plan
I wanted the shine, so I studied his hand —
the model is not the man

He'd talk about the house, the cars
the different women in his bed
They'd raise a glass and toast his name —
I wanted all of it in my head

There's a model man
polished front, no visible plan
I wanted the shine, so I studied his hand —
the model is not the man

I couldn't match his cars, his house
so I took the one that he'd cast aside
He never once cared for the cost
It cost me everything I had inside

There's a model man
polished front, no visible plan
I wanted the shine, so I studied his hand —
the model is not the man

Some model man

[Intro - hushed, admiring]

[Interlude - smoky, seductive build]

[Verse 3 - envious, admiring]
He'd talk about the house, the cars,
the different women in his bed.
They'd raise a glass and toast his name —
I wanted all of it in my head.

[Chorus - warm, seduced]
There's a model man,
polished front, no visible plan.
I wanted the shine, so I studied his hand —
the model is not the man.

[Bridge - stripped, desperate]
I couldn't match his cars, his house,
so I took the one that he'd cast aside.
He never once cared for the cost.
It cost me everything I had inside.

[Final Chorus - fuller, harder]
There's a model man,
polished front, no visible plan.
I wanted the shine, so I studied his hand —
the model is not the man.

[Outro - flat, bitter]
Some model man.

[End]

impression.text: This rock arrangement delivers a dense, anthemic texture paired with a nostalgic and dramatic emotional atmosphere. A high energy level propels the song forward, creating a driving arena-rock feel built on roaring electric guitars, a booming acoustic drum kit, and a gritty male lead vocal. The production quality balances a spacious reverberant mix with a thick wall-of-sound density, allowing the layered synthesizers and backing vocals to sit cohesively behind the commanding lead instruments. The explosive transition into the powerful chorus stands out as the track's defining moment, elevating the arrangement with soaring vocal harmonies and a striking surge in instrumental intensity.

review.review_text: The title track builds its case slow and mean, a 112 bpm 4/4 in E minor that starts hushed and admiring and ends flat with contempt: "Some model man." Rose is writing about envy as a slow poison, and the smartest line is the hook's own correction, "the model is not the man," which he lets you believe before pulling it out from under you. The arrangement promises smoky sax and brushed intimacy but reaches for arena scale instead, and the explosive lift into the final chorus lands like Springsteen circa The River, all soaring harmonies and a wall of guitar. That widescreen density is also the catch: the bridge, "It cost me everything I had inside," wants the room stripped bare, and the production keeps it too full to draw blood. A highlight that holds the room even when it overplays its hand.
